newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.03 rupees up at 42.70 to the dollar in the kerb market on Wednesday, but lost some ground after opening at 42.68 to the dollar, dealers said.
They said the rupee was likely to open steady on Thursday because of low supplies of the U.S. currency from Gulf states.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 6.70 percent, down from Tuesday's close at 6.75 percent.
